issue_context.title: Kublet calls to du can hang indefinitely
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

kubelet pod grew in size as it spawned an ever-increasing number of du child procs.

**What you expected to happen**:

This check should maybe timeout after a while.  Preferably before we spawn another du.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

I'm not quite sure unfortunately, I haven't seen this behavior first-hand.  I did get a report from a 3rd party about an end-user who experienced the behavior, and so I took a look at the code, and the behavior I would expect from du on a network filesystem that's not responding is that it would block indefinitely.

**Anything else we need to know?**:
I am new to the codebase but this looks like the culprit to me:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/23eb2180c65472f5c25fdec551b594f0b2db427d/pkg/volume/util/fs/fs.go#L71

I came across potentially related PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/74675

/sig node

That's certainly a way to get around du proc proliferation.  I'm afraid that stat call might block indefinitely leaving us with the same ultimate problem though.  IMO using `du` is convenient for a bunch of reasons.  Would it be acceptable to just invoke du under timeout(1)?  Is there a good way to set that timeout dynamically (i.e. is there some time interval constant that we can base our timeout value off of?)

review_comments:
I'm actually a little confused about how we can get into the state where there are lots of du's. 

The volume metrics are [gathered serially](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a6f209c1c038dce7256e1cf115ed393ec22fbb9e/pkg/kubelet/server/stats/volume_stat_calculator.go#L108), and the call to [JitterUntil](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a6f209c1c038dce7256e1cf115ed393ec22fbb9e/pkg/kubelet/server/stats/volume_stat_calculator.go#L64) is supposed to wait until the previous one completed.

/assign @gnufied 
to also help take a look

Sorry, I have one suspicion:
if we want to collect it serially, does [JitterUntil](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a6f209c1c038dce7256e1cf115ed393ec22fbb9e/pkg/kubelet/server/stats/volume_stat_calculator.go#L64) and [Forever](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a6f209c1c038dce7256e1cf115ed393ec22fbb9e/pkg/kubelet/server/stats/fs_resource_analyzer.go#L65) duplicated, or serial collect is protected by sync.Once safely?

We appear to be spinning one goroutine for each Pod on the node and that is what `Forever` does. But metric collection for each pod should be happening concurrently.  @gongguan which version of kube you are running?

Also - I am bit uncomfortable about using `bash` and random mix of `ps aux`. I know there are minor incompatiblities between versions.

> @gongguan which version of kube you are running?

I have met it in release-1.9 more than one year ago, [#88767](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/88767) remind me of that. However version haven't been mentioned in the issue.

> Also - I am bit uncomfortable about using `bash` and random mix of `ps aux`. I know there are minor incompatiblities between versions.

Actually, I haven't found a very good solution yet.
